title: Host & System Logs
description: Per-machine detail: CPU, memory, disk, network, thermals, hardware RAS (memory + GPU + SMART) and system logs.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Computed from the host's own clock (node_time_seconds), not the server's. Using time() instead would fold any clock skew between server and client into the reading, and would keep counting up after a machine stops reporting.

panels.title: Booted
panels.description: Wall-clock time of last boot. This is a Unix timestamp — it must be rendered as a date, not as a duration.

panels.title: Unit failures (24h)
panels.description: systemd unit failures counted from the log stream. node-exporter's systemd collector would give live unit state, but it needs D-Bus access that AppArmor denies to containers on stock Ubuntu, so it is off by default.

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Where the time actually goes. Sustained `iowait` points at storage, `steal` at a noisy neighbour on the hypervisor, `system` at kernel work.

panels.title: Swap & paging
panels.description: Swap in use. Pair with the pressure panel below — swap that is allocated but not being read back is harmless.

panels.title: Pressure stall (PSI)
panels.description: Fraction of time some task was stalled waiting for a resource. The most direct measure of contention there is — it detects pressure that utilisation percentages hide. Requires a kernel with PSI enabled.

panels.title: Disk latency
panels.description: Average service time per I/O. The `> 0` guard keeps an idle disk from dividing by zero and drawing a spike.

panels.title: Disk utilisation
panels.description: Percentage of wall time the device had at least one request in flight. Near 100% means the disk is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Physical interfaces only — loopback, veths and docker bridges are excluded so container traffic isn't double-counted.

panels.title: Errors & drops
panels.description: Anything sustained here is physical: cable, port, or duplex mismatch.

panels.title: File descriptors
panels.description: Against node_filefd_maximum. A steady climb is a descriptor leak.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: Every hwmon sensor the host exposes. Deliberately unfiltered: the chip naming for the CPU package sensor differs between AMD (k10temp), Intel (coretemp) and every board vendor, so pinning one chip pattern would leave most machines blank.

panels.title: CPU package power
panels.description: Intel RAPL. Not exposed on most AMD desktop parts.

panels.title: VRAM used
panels.description: DCGM reports framebuffer memory in MiB, so it is converted to bytes here rather than divided by 1e9.

panels.title: Throttling
panels.description: Fraction of time the GPU was clock-limited. DCGM counts violation time in microseconds, hence the 1e6 divisor.

panels.title: GPU DBE (uncorrectable)
panels.description: Double-bit ECC errors in VRAM — the GPU equivalent of a DIMM UE.

panels.title: Pending row remaps
panels.description: Pages awaiting retirement; a GPU reset is required to apply them.

panels.title: Last XID
panels.description: Most recent XID code reported by the driver. 48/63/64/92/94/95 indicate memory or hardware faults.

panels.title: PCIe replays
panels.description: A rising replay rate points at a marginal PCIe link — riser, slot, or seating.

panels.title: Since last CE
panels.description: The exporter reports NaN when the machine has never logged an event, so this shows `never` rather than a bogus 50-year age.

panels.title: CE rate (errors/hour)
panels.description: Corrected and uncorrected split apart — summing them would let a harmless CE trickle mask a single, far more serious UE.

panels.title: Top DIMMs (cumulative)
panels.description: Which physical DIMM the errors are on. This is the number you cross-check with `ras-mc-ctl --summary` before pulling hardware.

panels.title: EDAC (this boot)
panels.description: The kernel's own count, which resets at boot. rasdaemon's numbers above are cumulative across reboots; a mismatch is expected.

panels.title: Drive health
panels.description: Requires the client `smart` profile. `Health` is 1 for PASSED, 0 for FAILED. `Errors` is NVMe media errors, or reallocated sectors on SATA drives.

targets.expr: max by (machine, device) (smartctl_device_media_errors{machine=~"$machine"}) or max by (machine, device) (smartctl_device_attribute{machine=~"$machine",attribute_name="Reallocated_Sector_Ct",attribute_value_type="raw"})

panels.title: Log lines/s
panels.description: Zero here while metrics still flow means the log transport broke; see the Collection Health dashboard.

panels.title: Error lines by program
panels.description: Errors only. (This panel previously charted syslog_lines_total — every line, not just the errors.)

panels.title: Kernel MCE / hardware errors
panels.description: Not restricted to program="kernel": the journal reports the identifier as `kernel`, but rsyslog on some distros attributes these lines differently.

targets.expr: {job="syslog", machine=~"$machine", program=~"kernel|.*"} |~ "(?i)(mce|machine check|hardware error|edac|memory failure|uncorrectable|corrected error)"
